topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the scope of the lecture, framing how mutations, cellular origins, and the microenvironment drive cancer evolution alongside key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Genetic Clonal Selection and Epigenetic Regulation
topics.groupedBecause: They examine how successive genetic mutations and non-mutational epigenetic alterations drive clonal selection and phenotypic changes during tumor progression.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Stem Cell Hierarchies
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the role of normal tissue hierarchies and stemness in tumor initiation across models of leukemia and colorectal cancer.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and Inflammatory Drivers of Cancer Progression
topics.groupedBecause: They illustrate how environmental promoters, inflammatory signaling, and supportive stroma provide permissive conditions necessary for mutated cells to form and sustain tumors.

topics.label: Techniques for Investigating Tumor Evolution and Microenvironments
topics.groupedBecause: It details contemporary genomic, transcriptomic, and spatial mapping technologies used to study tumor heterogeneity and cellular interactions.

topics.label: Integrated Evolutionary Model of Cancer and Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: They synthesise the interconnected genetic, cellular, and microenvironmental factors governing cancer evolution and conclude the lecture.
